name: @hydranium/glsp-client
description: Host-neutral client classes for GLSP heads built on @hydranium/glsp-server, the binder that mounts them in a Theia frontend, a VS Code webview or a plain browser page, the one call that mounts a diagram in a page, and the edge whose labels keep finite bounds without bendpoints.

scripts.prepack: node -e "const m=require('./package.json'),fs=require('node:fs');const missing=[m.main,...Object.values(m.bin||{})].filter(entry=>entry&&!fs.existsSync(entry));if(missing.length){console.error('prepack '+m.name+': not built ('+missing.join(', ')+' missing). Run the build before packing: a files entry that matches nothing is skipped silently, so the tarball would ship src only.');process.exit(1);}"

//exports: The stylesheet key is an asset entry, spelled as the exact filename so nothing becomes reachable automatically. It lets an adopter `@import` the sheet, re-bundle it or override it by specifier. `tsc` emits no assets, and `check:exports` asserts the file exists and ships through `files`.
//peerDependencies: `inversify` is imported plainly, as `@eclipse-glsp/client` imports it, and peered so the classes here decorate with the same copy the diagram container resolves; `@theia/core/shared/inversify` re-exports that copy, so a Theia frontend satisfies it without a second install. `snabbdom` is a peer for the `VNode` type the hidden-bounds updater reads, the same reason the Theia package peers it.
//prepack: The publish guard, a `prepack` rather than a `prepare`: `prepack` runs only when a tarball is made (`npm pack`, `npm publish`) and never on install, so it cannot break the install it has no business touching. What it defends against: `files` lists `lib`, `lib` is gitignored, and a `files` entry matching nothing is skipped SILENTLY — so `npm publish` from an unbuilt tree emits a tarball of `src` and nothing else, with no error.
//sideEffects: A stylesheet IS the side effect: `style/message-overlay.css` is pulled in by a bare import in `message-overlay.js`, and a CSS module exports nothing, so under a blanket `false` a bundler drops the import as unused and the diagram's messages render unstyled. Nothing fails at build time.
